g.text: Property Vocabulary
Hardness — resistance to indentation / wear; not the same as toughness.
Strength — resistance to applied load / stress before failure or deformation, depending on property.
Toughness — ability to absorb energy before fracture.
Ductility — ability to plastically deform / elongate before fracture.
Brittleness — tendency to fracture with little plastic deformation.
Thermal conductivity — ability to conduct heat.
Instructor cue: property word first → evidence → consequence. Do not jump to grade-specific claims.
This is prerequisite vocabulary, not the formal iron-carbon/transformation sequence.
Material Comparison Matrix — Baseline Only
CARBON STEEL — typically magnetic; properties/weldability vary with composition and condition; exact grade controls.
STAINLESS STEEL — family/alloy dependent; chromium is associated with corrosion resistance; contamination control matters.
ALUMINUM — low density; high thermal conductivity; oxide layer requires attention; exact alloy/temper controls.
Samples/photos support observation. They do NOT establish exact grade, alloy, temper, or procedure.
Use authorized source documentation before making an exact material/property claim.
Behavior Scenarios
1) Must bend before breaking → which property?
2) Must absorb impact energy → which property?
3) Rapidly carries heat away from the weld zone → which property?
4) Surface resists indentation → which property?
For each: PROPERTY → WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS → WHAT YOU CANNOT CONCLUDE.
Exact material grade/alloy/temper comes from source documentation, not visual guessing.
DAY 6 RULE: OBSERVE → CHECK SOURCE → STATE ONLY WHAT THE SOURCE SUPPORTS.
